prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) validates authority/mode/interlocks/availability, commands/compares indications, flags discrepancies, associates Breaker Inspection Tag, uses Battery Load Test Record, sends Bay Status Digest→Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing). North Bay Controller blocks unready closes/preserves local control during supervisory loss; South Bay Controller reports mode/availability; scopes non-substitutable. North Protection Panel maintains independent zone/trip paths; Transformer Protection Panel independently protects transformers. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) supplies quality-checked time/Clock Drift Snapshot→Sequence Event Archive (Orchard), retaining authoritative events/control outcomes/testing/restoration. Engineering Workstation provides authorized revision-controlled review/configuration/export, produces Settings Review Receipt→Maintenance Remote Terminal (maintenance-only; no bypass). Station DC System monitors supplies/abnormal loss, retains Battery Load Test Record. Control Room Operator requests switching, reviews/acknowledges alarms, records actions/restrictions, tracks disabled protection until verified restoration, produces Clearance Handoff Memo. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) checks prerequisites/conflicts/clearances, maintains switching sequence, produces Isolation Boundary Card/confirms handback. Substation Supervisor authorizes/escalates, controls communication/mapping/logic/configuration changes, coordinates timing/responsibilities with Keystone. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) reviews settings/coordination/events/test scope/restoration. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) locally verifies identity/status/boundaries, produces Breaker Inspection Tag(condition/time), reports discrepancies/unsafe conditions; work requires confirmed clearance/isolation/grounding. Requirements: plan maintenance for loading/switching/staffing; approved tests/calibrated instruments/stop means; inhibit uncertain/nonpermissive remote commands; degraded indications unavailable pending verification; manual operation requires procedures/local checks/operator communication. Preserve rejection context, bounded authority/local precedence, ordered switching/holds/stops, abnormal discrepancies, source/order/time/quality/uncertainty; time

S219: Restoration includes confirming normal indications, protection availability, communications status, and the removal of temporary test connections.

S222: The Control Room Operator remains responsible for deciding whether an automation request is appropriate for current operating conditions.
S223: The Bay Automation Controller shall execute only commands permitted by its approved logic and configured interlocks.
S224: The Feeder Protection Relay shall retain its protective function independently of supervisory communications.
S225: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection behavior after material changes and records any unresolved concerns for operational follow-up.
S226: The Station Supervisory Control System presents control indications and command results for operator assessment.
S227: The Sequence Event Archive retains time-ordered records needed to reconstruct significant control and protection events.
S228: The Engineering Workstation shall be used for authorized configuration work under established change control.
S229: The Satellite Time Receiver supports consistent event timing, and time-quality concerns shall be investigated before records are relied upon for sequence analysis.
S230: The Station Gateway shall maintain the defined boundary between station automation and external communications.
S231: The Station DC System shall be confirmed available before switching that depends on station control power.
S232: The Breaker Control Unit shall reject commands that do not satisfy its configured permissive conditions.
S233: Substation Field Crew uses the Isolation Boundary Card to verify the approved work boundary before entering the controlled area.
S234: Substation Field Crew reports unexpected equipment conditions promptly and pauses work when the approved boundary is uncertain.
S235: Switching Desk Coordinator receives the Clearance Handoff Memo and confirms that its clearance status agrees with the active switching record.
S236: Keystone shall confirm that switching authority, equipment state, and communication limits are understood before coordinating any automation-enabled action.

S238: The Control Room Operator confirms indications locally when remote status is incomplete, inconsistent, or delayed.
S239: The Protection Relay Engineer assesses unexplained trips and abnormal protection indications before protection is returned to service.
